speaker: Leonard
text: Our whole universe was in a hot dense state, then nearly 14 billion years ago, expansion started. Wait, the Earth began to cool, the autotrophs began to drool, Neanderthals developed tools, we built a wall. We built the pyramids, science, history, unraveling the mystery that all started with the Big Bang.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Who's running the red Corvette? That would be me. You know, in the future, when we're disembodied brains in jars, we're going to look back on this as eight hours well wasted.

speaker: Benny
text: I don't want to be in a jar. I want my brain in an android body. Eight feet tall and ripped. I suppose you could have your android penis circumcised. But that's something your rabbi would have to discuss with the manufacturer.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I promised my mother.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Not to mention you'd have to power down on Saturdays.

speaker: Leonard
text: Um, why is this letter in the trash?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, there's always the possibility that a trash can spontaneously formed around the letter, but Occam's razor would suggest that someone threw it out.

speaker: Leonard
text: It's from the Institute for Experimental Physics. They want us to present our paper on the properties of super solids at the topical conference on Bose-Einstein condensates.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I know. I read it before I threw it out.

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay, if I may drill down to the bedrock of my question, why did you throw it out?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Because I have no interest in standing in the rose room of the Pasadena Marriott in front of a group of judgmental strangers who wouldn't recognize true genius if it were standing in front of them giving a speech. Which if I were there, it would be.

speaker: Raj
text: I'm with you. I just have to make sure if I'm a synthetic human that I'd still be Jewish. I don't know, Sheldon, those topical conference on Bose-Einstein condensates parties are legendary.

speaker: Leonard
text: Forget the parties.

speaker: Raj
text: Forget the parties, what a nerd.

speaker: Leonard
text: Are there any other honors I've gotten that I don't know about? Did UPS drop off a Nobel Prize with my name on it?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Leonard, please don't take this the wrong way, but the day you win a Nobel Prize is the day I begin my research on the drag coefficient of tassels on flying carpets.

speaker: Benny
text: The only thing you took from that insult was your mama.

speaker: Raj
text: I got one.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Hey Leonard, your mama's research methodology is so flawed.

speaker: Leonard
text: Shut up, Howard. Sheldon, we have to do this.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, we don't. We have to take in nourishment, expel waste, and inhale enough oxygen to keep ourselves from dying. Everything else is optional.

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay, let me put it this way. I'm doing it.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You can't. I'm the lead author.

speaker: Leonard
text: Oh, come on. The only reason you're the lead author is because we went alphabetically.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I let you think we went alphabetically to spare you the humiliation of dealing with the fact that it was my idea. Not to put too fine a point on it, but I was throwing you a bone. You're welcome.

speaker: Leonard
text: Excuse me, I designed the experiment that proved the hypothesis.

speaker: Sheldon
text: It doesn't mean proving.

speaker: Leonard
text: So the entire scientific community is just supposed to take your word?

speaker: Sheldon
text: They're not supposed to, but they should.

speaker: Leonard
text: Alright, I don't care what you say. I'm going to the conference and I'm presenting our findings.

speaker: Sheldon
text: And I forbid it.

speaker: Leonard
text: You forbid it?

speaker: Sheldon
text: If I'm not taking credit for our work, then nobody is.

speaker: Leonard
text: So you admit that it's our work?

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, once again, I'm throwing you a bone. And once again, you are welcome.

speaker: Leonard
text: Oh no, he didn't.
